2026

at the Brewhouse & Kitchen, 2a Corsica Street, London, N5 1JJ

Date Artist Note
29th October 2026 Louise and Chris Rogan Both fine singers in close family harmonies, this father-daughter duo, with Louise on piano and Chris on stringed instruments, perform their combination of traditional and original songs. They have played and headlined major festival stages and their album 'Things That Matter' has won rave reviews. Louise has also released a solo album. Immensely good.
‘... nothing quite prepared me for the quality of Louise's vocals and the wonderful on-set chemistry of the combination’ Rory Stanbridge, FATEA
5th November 2026 Dana Robinson Americana-roots and folk all the way from Cabot, Vermont.
Dana brings us his original songwriting and traditional Appalachian music with mighty fine accompaniment from banjo, mandolin, and guitar.
12th November 2026 Robb Johnson Bastion of the left and a fine writer of songs both political and personal, Robb is a witty, angry and passionate performer with one foot in 70s punk and the other in the chansonnier tradition of Jacques Brel. Ever popular—especially in Belgium.
‘An English original.’ Robin Denselow, The Guardian.
19th November 2026 Mat Green and Andy Turner Traditional English dance tunes brilliantly played on fiddle and Anglo concertina. Re-worked tunes from the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries are a feature. Andy sings and Mat may dance (whilst still playing the fiddle).
26th November 2026 Hunter Muskett Acoustic/electric three-piece playing distinctive original songs in a folky, bluesy, sometimes Americana vein.
Harmonies, guitar, bass, mandolin, and 50-odd years on the folk scene.
‘...a creative musical force up there with the very best.’ David Pratt FATEA
3rd December 2026 Elsie Franklin and the Rockettes Acoustic country blues from an all-female trio, with Elsie Franklin on resonator guitar and vocals, Francesca Shaw on double bass, and Roni Reeds on drums and washboard. Prepare for driving rhythms and 'no time for talking or anecdoting', just music!
‘Elsie Franklin is the most natural blues singer I’ve heard in years. Her guitar playing is pretty damn good, too, uncluttered and tasteful, she really understands the genre–she’s the whole package.’ Dave Kelly, The Blues Band
10th December 2026 John Hegley The Bard of Luton returns with tales of his grandma, bungalows and guillemots. Come early to avoid sitting in the front row. Audience participation obligatory.
‘Marvellous, joyful fun’ The Daily Telegraph
‘An incurable entertainer’ The Guardian
17th December 2026 Christmas Party and Singaround After a feast of entertainment, it's time to make your own fun.
Bring songs, tunes, and obscure instruments.
24th December 2026 Club closed Happy Christmas!
31st December 2026 Club closed Happy New Year!

2027

at the Brewhouse & Kitchen, 2a Corsica Street, London, N5 1JJ

Date Artist Note
7th January 2027 Luke Daniels Ace melodeon player (and multi-instrumentalist) Luke Daniels has a list of high-profile credits to his name, working with Riverdance, Jethro Tull, De Dannan, and Cara Dillon, but has also made twelve solo albums. From an album of melodeon music transcribed from early wax cylinders and 78s to electronic music to performing at the Royal Festival Hall with the London Philharmonic Orchestra to writing many songs, expect a set drawing from an incredibly varied body of work.
14th January 2027 London Klezmer Quartet Founded in 2009, through four albums, line-up changes, and international moves, the London Klezmer Quartet is known far beyond London, playing regularly in Europe and all over the world. Susi Evans on clarinet, Szilvia Csaranko on accordion, Flora Curzon on violin, and Indra Buraczewska on double bass are all superb musicians, with Indra’s distinctive alto voice interpreting songs in a way that you will remember for a long time.
‘While the arrangements are acoustic and traditional, the playing is energetic and fresh.’ Simon Broughton, London Evening Standard
21st January 2027 Linda Moylan Born in Waterford and brought up in London’s East End, Linda Moylan is a wonderful singer who has released two albums so far (The Merchant, produced by Phil Beer (2021), and The Fool (2024)). Her songwriting has drawn widespread acclaim, but she is firmly rooted in the tradition, too, and has put together a cohesive repertoire of old and new. She will be accompanied by Ian Montague on guitar and Rebecca Mileham on violin.
‘[S]he’s the owner of a unique, vivid and absolutely alluring voice that’s capable of taking a multiplicity of forms, from the sultry, the bluesy, the smoky to the unbelievably sweet—often during the same song.’ John Barlass, At the Barrier
28th January 2027 Scottish evening with Duncan Menzies and friends Duncan Menzies is an outstanding Scottish fiddler and piper. Adam Beattie on vocals and guitar has his roots in Scottish folk music and is an accomplished songwriter. After a great evening at the club last year, Duncan and Adam are joined by Will Chamberlain (Club Débris and Brown Boots Boogie Band) who plays piano with energy, drive and a sense of fun. Bring Scottish songs, dance tunes and poems and revel in Scotland’s amazing contribution to world culture.
